sentences.text: The single known species, Apsaravis ukhaana, was named by Mark Norell and Jack Clarke in 2001.
This creature shows a mix of primitive bird features from the Sauriurae group and advanced traits like at least ten sacral vertebrae and a patellar groove on the femur.
It holds the distinction of being the most primitive bird known to possess an extensor process, a bony projection that helps automate wing extension during flight.
Despite these innovations, it retained narrow intercondylar grooves and barrel-shaped tibiotarsal condyles shared with early theropods.
Fossils were found in the Camel's Humps sublocality of the Djadokhta Formation at Ukhaa Tolgod in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia.
Phylogenetic analysis places Apsaravis as the most basal member of the Ornithurae lineage, making it more advanced than Enantiornithes and Patagopteryx.
Living approximately 78 million years ago during the Campanian age, it inhabited a very arid, open landscape that was likely hotter than today with intermittent rainfall.
Scientists debate whether this discovery means the group Enantiornithes is paraphyletic, suggesting these birds were actually ancestors to modern birds rather than a separate side branch.
